title: Pumped hydro permitting and siting limits
bottleneck: Pumped hydro is the cheapest bulk storage where it exists, but new sites face a decade of permitting, environmental opposition over water and land use, and transmission distance to loads. Closed-loop off-river designs reduce environmental impact but still need elevation difference and water rights. The US has a large pipeline of proposed projects and almost no completions.
why_it_blocks: The best storage technology by cost and lifetime is throttled by process, not physics. Permitting timelines longer than technology lifetimes stall the pipeline.
current_state: FERC has dozens of preliminary permits outstanding. Few projects reach construction amid environmental review and financing hurdles. Developers increasingly propose closed-loop designs sited away from rivers, but these still face multi-year federal licensing and local opposition over land use.
